Richardson, Plano, and Frisco can cost less and offer more space, but they require a daily highway commute. ::: ## **Apartment Search** {#finding-an-apartment} From locating a unit to understanding your first bill, these are the main things that make Dallas apartment hunting different from other cities. ### **Where to Search for Apartments** {#apartment-search}
Apartments.com Zillow Apartment List

```
Tour in person when possible because quality can vary significantly within the same price range, especially in Uptown high-rises. A common starting guideline is to budget about 25–30% of income for rent. ::: {.callout-important} Always ask about move-in specials before signing. Apartment locators may also know about unpublished specials or availability. ::: ## **Fees, Deposits, and Move-In Deals** {#move-in-deals} Winter, especially November through February, is generally the slowest leasing season and the best time to negotiate. Summer is peak demand and usually has fewer concessions. However, it's important to note the more common move-in deals that you may see during your apartment search process ### **Deals on Housing** | Area or Property Type | Typical Deal Level | What to Expect | |---|---|---| | Uptown and New High-Rises | Biggest deals | One to two-and-a-half months of free rent may be available when buildings are competing to fill new units. | | Frisco and Las Colinas | Biggest deals | Newer high-rise and mid-rise buildings often offer aggressive incentives. | | Richardson, Addison, and Older Plano Properties | Smaller but still useful | Waived administrative fees or reduced deposits are more common than large rent concessions. | ### **Apartment Fees** {#apartment-fees} Always ask for the **total effective monthly cost**, not only the advertised base rent. | Fee | Typical Cost | |---|---| | Administrative Fee | $150–$300 | | Application Fee | $50–$75 per person | | Amenity or Valet Trash Fee | $20–$30 per month | | Pet Rent | $20–$35 per month, plus deposit | | RUBS Utility Billing | Shared water and trash charges | | Security Deposit | | Garage Parking | $100–$200 per month (depends) | :::{.callout-important} Always ask about move-in specials before signing. Apartment locators may also know about unpublished specials or availability. ::: ## **Electricity** {#electricity} Texas has a deregulated electricity market. Use [PowerToChoose.org](https://www.powertochoose.org/){target="_blank"}, the official Public Utility Commission of Texas comparison site, to compare plans by ZIP code. - Start with a fixed-rate 12-month plan for more predictable billing. - Compare the all-in rate at 1,000 kWh, not only the advertised teaser rate. - Oncor delivers the electricity and reads the meter regardless of which retail provider you select. - Air conditioning may run almost continuously during summer, so budget for higher electric bills from June through September. ::: ::: {.section-dark} # Getting Around Dallas {#parking-and-transportation} Uptown high-rises commonly charge **$100–$200 per month** for a reserved garage space, although some properties include surface parking. Suburban complexes in Plano, Frisco, and Richardson are more likely to include parking at no extra cost. However, previous GLP classes have emphasized the need to make sure whether the parking is inside the apartment complex or not! ::: {.panel-tabset} ## **Driving Through Dallas** {#driving-through-dallas} ### Major Highways ::: {.callout-tip} # **Transportation Rule of Thumb** US-75 is the route most associated with unpredictable congestion. The Dallas North Tollway is often more reliable but costs money via Toll Tag. :::
```{=html}

US-75 / Central Expressway

Pros
  • Direct route through Uptown to Richardson and Plano
  • Many DART stations are located along the corridor
Cons
  • Frequently congested throughout the day
  • Narrow lanes and recurring construction can cause delays

I-35E / Stemmons Freeway

Pros
  • Direct connection toward Las Colinas, Irving, and Fort Worth
Cons
  • Heavy freight traffic
  • Frequent backups near the Design District and Mockingbird Lane

I-635 / LBJ Freeway

Pros
  • Managed TEXpress toll lanes can remain faster during rush hour
Cons
  • Free lanes are often congested
  • Toll-lane costs can add up

Dallas North Tollway

Pros
  • Usually the fastest route north to Addison, Plano, Frisco, and the Legacy area
  • Often more reliable than US-75 during rush hour
Cons
  • It is a toll road
  • Daily commuting costs can accumulate quickly
``` ## **Public Transit and TollTag** {#dart-tolltag} | Item | Cost | Notes | |---|---:|---| | ***DART (Three Hour Pass)*** | $3.00 | Valid for 2.5 hours. Purchase through the GoPass app. | | ***DART (Day Pass)*** | $6.00 | Unlimited rides on rail, buses, and GoLink for the day. Confirm current pricing in the app. | | ***NTTA TollTag*** | Free Registration + Lower Toll Rates | Used for cashless tollways, including the DNT, President George Bush Turnpike, DFW Air and SH-161. It can also be used for parking at the DFW Airport. | The Dallas–Fort Worth area offers two primary ways to get around: DART for public transportation and the NTTA TollTag for driving on toll roads. * **DART (Dallas Area Rapid Transit)**: DFW's public transportation system, providing light rail, buses, streetcars, and GoLink on-demand services throughout DFW; utilizes the GoPass app; convenient option for commuting without a car. * **NTTA TollTag**: Free electronic toll collection sticker issued by the North Texas Tollway Authority; allows drivers to pay tolls automatically on participating toll roads without stopping; typically provides lower toll rates than paying by mail. ## **Airports** {#airports} ```{=html}

DFW International Airport

Best for: International travel, widest selection of flights

Drive from Uptown: Approximately 25–40 minutes

Airline strength: Major American Airlines hub

Flight mix: International and domestic

Dallas Love Field

Drive from Uptown: Approximately 10–15 minutes

Airline strength: Southwest Airlines' home base

Flight mix: Mostly domestic and short-haul

``` ::: ::: ::: {.section-light} # Getting Settled in Texas Getting settled in Texas means preparing for the weather and checking a few practical tasks off your list. Explore the tabs below for what to expect throughout the year, how to register your vehicle and update your driver's license, and other details to help you feel at home in Dallas. ::: {.panel-tabset} ## **Weather in Texas** {#weather}
### Summer
95–105°F
Hot and humid from roughly June through September. Air conditioning runs nearly nonstop, and electricity bills can rise substantially.
### Fall
Best Weather
October and November usually bring warm days, cooler nights, and lower humidity. Generally the most pleasant time of year.
### Winter
40s–60s°F
Usually mild but unpredictable. Ice storms or hard freezes can shut down roads and schools. Keep a coat and blanket in your car.
### Spring
Storm Season
Spring is beautiful but volatile. Severe thunderstorms and tornadoes are possible, so keep weather alerts enabled.
## **Register Your Vehicle** {#vehicle-registration} Texas requires new residents to register their vehicle within 30 days of moving to the state. For most GLPers living in Dallas, this process will be completed through the Dallas County tax assessor-collector's office. ### **Follow This Order** The order matters. Complete these steps before applying for your Texas driver's license: 1. **Confirm Texas-compliant auto insurance** 2. **Complete an emissions inspection**, if required for your county 3. **Register and title your vehicle** at your county tax office 4. **Apply for your Texas driver's license** through Texas DPS Dallas County is an emissions-testing county, so most applicable non-commercial vehicles must pass an emissions inspection before registration. Texas eliminated the general safety inspection requirement for most non-commercial vehicles in 2025. ### **If a Parent Is Gifting You the Vehicle** If your vehicle is currently titled in a parent's name and they are transferring it to you as a gift, complete the **Affidavit of Motor Vehicle Gift Transfer (Form 14-317)** as part of the title-transfer process. A qualifying gift between a parent and child is generally subject to a **$10 Texas motor vehicle gift tax** rather than the standard motor vehicle sales tax. Both the donor and recipient must sign the required gift-transfer documents, and the paperwork is submitted through the county tax office. Bring the documents required for your situation, which may include: - Out-of-state title or other proof of ownership - Application for Texas Title and/or Registration (Form 130-U) - Affidavit of Motor Vehicle Gift Transfer (Form 14-317), if applicable - Proof of insurance that meets Texas minimums - Photo identification - Vehicle Inspection Report, if the inspection is not already available electronically ::: {.callout-important} ### **Plan Ahead for Appointments** DMV, county tax office, inspection, and DPS appointment availability can fill up quickly, especially around busy moving periods. Check appointment requirements and availability as soon as you know your move date rather than waiting until your first week in Dallas. ::: ## **Emissions Inspection** {#emissions-inspection} ### Complete an Emissions Inspection {#emissions-inspection} Dallas County requires qualifying vehicles to pass an emissions inspection before registration. Texas eliminated the general safety inspection requirement for most non-commercial vehicles in 2025, but emissions testing still applies in Dallas and several other Texas counties. ## **Driver's License** {#license} After completing your vehicle requirements, schedule your Texas driver's license appointment through the Texas Department of Public Safety. Completing the vehicle process first helps ensure you have the Texas registration documentation needed as you establish residency. ### Getting a Texas Driver's License {#texas-drivers-license} Apply through the Texas Department of Public Safety. Bring: - Proof of identity - Social Security number - Two proofs of Texas residency ## **Optional Registrations** ### Register to Vote {#register-to-vote} You may register when obtaining a Texas ID or through the appropriate state registration process. ### Texas Minimum Auto Liability Coverage {#auto-insurance} | Coverage | Minimum | |---|---:| | Bodily injury per person | $30,000 | | Bodily injury per accident | $60,000 | | Property damage | $25,000 | This is commonly summarized as **30/60/25**. Confirm that your out-of-state policy meets these minimums before registering your vehicle. ::: ::: ::: {.section-dark} # Getting Set Up in the Office {#getting-set-up-in-the-office} The Dallas office is a vibrant and welcoming environment where new employees can quickly feel at home and connected to the team. Our team is committed to providing a supportive and collaborative workspace that helps everyone thrive. With that being said, it's important that we follow the rules and expectations set within the office space by listening to some words of advice from PMG's Head of Culture, Pam Buyers! ::: {.panel-tabset} ## **Office Expectations** {#office-expectations} - **Communication & Engagement**: Keep volume down in common areas to avoid disturbing others or leaking sensitive discussions, stay on top of your emails and Slack messages, and stay actively engaged during meetings (including turning your camera on during Zoom calls). - **Kitchen & Shared Spaces**: Clean up after yourself immediately—wash your own dishes, wipe down microwaves after spills, clear your table after eating, and throw away any stray trash you see. Be mindful of strong-smelling foods like fish or Brussels sprouts when bringing lunch. - **Shared Food & Perks**: Wait until everyone has had a chance to get food before taking seconds or packing leftovers. - **Health & Courtesy**: Stay home when you are feeling sick to keep the rest of the team healthy. - **Meeting & Desk Management**: Always reserve a desk ahead of time (especially when visiting another office), and end meetings on time so the next group can start promptly ## **What to Wear** {#what-to-wear} **What to Wear (The Dos):** - **Express Yourself Comfortably**: Wear outfits that make you feel confident and authentic, including visible tattoos (work-appropriate), piercings, and colorful hair. - **Adapt to Your Audience**: Match your personal style with the expectations of the client or partner you're meeting with. **What Not to Wear (The Don'ts):** - **Avoid Unprofessional Attire**: Skip clothing that is overly revealing, shows your midriff, is excessively short, or is overly baggy. Aim for smart casual. - **Ditch the Sleepwear**: Save pajama pants for home and opt for elevated joggers or comfortable, neat alternatives instead. - **Keep It Respectful**: Never wear items featuring offensive text or graphics. ## **Benefits** {#benefits} ::: ::: ::: {.section-light} # PMGer Recommendations {#pmger-recommendations} Pulled straight from a PMG survey — the spots and tips real coworkers actually use.

Browse food, coffee, bars, and things to do recommended by fellow PMGers. Open the full list for locations, links, and their tips.

Loading recommendations...
::: ::: {.section-dark} # Final Checklist {#checklist} ## PMG Pre-Engagement {#pmg-pre-engagement} - [ ] Ask the P&C Team for additional onboarding recommendations - [ ] Review PMGer apartment and neighborhood suggestions - [ ] Confirm first-day office details - [ ] Save important PMG contacts ## Your First Week in Dallas {#setup-checklist} ### Before Move-In - [ ] Set Up Electricity - [ ] Purchase Renter's Insurance - [ ] Confirm Parking and Move-In Instructions ### First Few Days - [ ] Set up your TollTag - [ ] Download GoPass - [ ] Test Your Commute to the PMG office - [ ] Locate Your Nearest Grocery Store, Pharmacy, and Gas Station ### First Month - [ ] Complete emissions inspection if required - [ ] Register your vehicle - [ ] Begin the Texas driver's license process ```{=html} ``` ::: :::

Texas eliminated the general safety inspection requirement for most non-commercial vehicles in 2025. ### **If a Parent Is Gifting You the Vehicle** If your vehicle is currently titled in a parent's name and they are transferring it to you as a gift, complete the **Affidavit of Motor Vehicle Gift Transfer (Form 14-317)** as part of the title-transfer process. A qualifying gift between a parent and child is generally subject to a **$10 Texas motor vehicle gift tax** rather than the standard motor vehicle sales tax. Both the donor and recipient must sign the required gift-transfer documents, and the paperwork is submitted through the county tax office. Bring the documents required for your situation, which may include: - Out-of-state title or other proof of ownership - Application for Texas Title and/or Registration (Form 130-U) - Affidavit of Motor Vehicle Gift Transfer (Form 14-317), if applicable - Proof of insurance that meets Texas minimums - Photo identification - Vehicle Inspection Report, if the inspection is not already available electronically ::: {.callout-important} ### **Plan Ahead for Appointments** DMV, county tax office, inspection, and DPS appointment availability can fill up quickly, especially around busy moving periods. Check appointment requirements and availability as soon as you know your move date rather than waiting until your first week in Dallas. ::: ## **Emissions Inspection** {#emissions-inspection} ### Complete an Emissions Inspection {#emissions-inspection} Dallas County requires qualifying vehicles to pass an emissions inspection before registration. Texas eliminated the general safety inspection requirement for most non-commercial vehicles in 2025, but emissions testing still applies in Dallas and several other Texas counties. ## **Driver's License** {#license} After completing your vehicle requirements, schedule your Texas driver's license appointment through the Texas Department of Public Safety. Completing the vehicle process first helps ensure you have the Texas registration documentation needed as you establish residency. ### Getting a Texas Driver's License {#texas-drivers-license} Apply through the Texas Department of Public Safety. Bring: - Proof of identity - Social Security number - Two proofs of Texas residency ## **Optional Registrations** ### Register to Vote {#register-to-vote} You may register when obtaining a Texas ID or through the appropriate state registration process. ### Texas Minimum Auto Liability Coverage {#auto-insurance} | Coverage | Minimum | |---|---:| | Bodily injury per person | $30,000 | | Bodily injury per accident | $60,000 | | Property damage | $25,000 | This is commonly summarized as **30/60/25**. Confirm that your out-of-state policy meets these minimums before registering your vehicle. ::: ::: ::: {.section-dark} # Getting Set Up in the Office {#getting-set-up-in-the-office} The Dallas office is a vibrant and welcoming environment where new employees can quickly feel at home and connected to the team. Our team is committed to providing a supportive and collaborative workspace that helps everyone thrive. With that being said, it's important that we follow the rules and expectations set within the office space by listening to some words of advice from PMG's Head of Culture, Pam Buyers! ::: {.panel-tabset} ## **Office Expectations** {#office-expectations} - **Communication & Engagement**: Keep volume down in common areas to avoid disturbing others or leaking sensitive discussions, stay on top of your emails and Slack messages, and stay actively engaged during meetings (including turning your camera on during Zoom calls). - **Kitchen & Shared Spaces**: Clean up after yourself immediately—wash your own dishes, wipe down microwaves after spills, clear your table after eating, and throw away any stray trash you see. Be mindful of strong-smelling foods like fish or Brussels sprouts when bringing lunch. - **Shared Food & Perks**: Wait until everyone has had a chance to get food before taking seconds or packing leftovers. - **Health & Courtesy**: Stay home when you are feeling sick to keep the rest of the team healthy. - **Meeting & Desk Management**: Always reserve a desk ahead of time (especially when visiting another office), and end meetings on time so the next group can start promptly ## **What to Wear** {#what-to-wear} **What to Wear (The Dos):** - **Express Yourself Comfortably**: Wear outfits that make you feel confident and authentic, including visible tattoos (work-appropriate), piercings, and colorful hair. - **Adapt to Your Audience**: Match your personal style with the expectations of the client or partner you're meeting with. **What Not to Wear (The Don'ts):** - **Avoid Unprofessional Attire**: Skip clothing that is overly revealing, shows your midriff, is excessively short, or is overly baggy. Aim for smart casual. - **Ditch the Sleepwear**: Save pajama pants for home and opt for elevated joggers or comfortable, neat alternatives instead. - **Keep It Respectful**: Never wear items featuring offensive text or graphics. ## **Benefits** {#benefits} ::: ::: ::: {.section-light} # PMGer Recommendations {#pmger-recommendations} Pulled straight from a PMG survey — the spots and tips real coworkers actually use.
